plan.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill passes its heart-safety test vs insulin glargine in type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4, The Lancet)
plan.angle: Title: 'Is the Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill Safe for the Heart? ACHIEVE-4 vs Insulin Glargine #shorts'. Answer: 'In about 2,700 adults with type 2 diabetes plus overweight or obesity at higher heart risk, followed for about 2 years, it was not worse than insulin glargine for major heart events: 4.2% vs 5.0%, HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20.' Explain that non-inferior means 'not worse', not 'proven better'. The death signal (HR 0.43) is nominal, so a hint, not proof. Limits: open-label, compared with insulin rather than placebo, Lilly-funded. Approval status hedged as of Sept 2026. Exact prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Is the Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill Safe for Your Heart? ACHIEVE-4 vs Insulin #shorts
plan.why: Published in the Lancet on 30 Sep and hasn't reached consumers yet. Foundayo is a newly searched brand, and our orforglipron long-form had the top views. It also does evidence literacy (non-inferior ≠ better), which covers the myth-busting share. | fact-check: Verified: ACHIEVE-4 was published in The Lancet (2026). It was open-label, non-inferiority and active-comparator (insulin glargine), with 2,749 randomised: 1,371 to orforglipron and 1,378 to glargine. Median follow-up was about 2 years. MACE-4 occurred in 57/1,358 (4.2%) vs 67/1,343 (5.0%), HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.59–1.20), and non-inferiority was met. All-cause death HR was 0.43 (95% CI 0.25–0.75), nominal P=.002, so it's hypothesis-generating. Fixes: (1) The population is adults with T2D AND overweight or obesity at increased cardiovascular risk. Add 'overweight or obesity'. (2) Use the analysed n from the Lancet paper (1,358 + 1,343 in the primary analysis) and say which n you're using. (3) MACE-4 includes hospitalisation for unstable angina, so define it, not just 'heart attack and stroke'. (4) Foundayo approval status: US approval for obesity in April 2026 and UK in August 2026 per the coverage. Don't imply it is approved for T2D unless you confirm that, and hedge with 'as of Sept 2026'. (5) Generic name first. Foundayo is orforglipron's brand, so using it is OK for recognition. (6) Put the absolute rates (4.2% vs 5.0%) next to the HR.

package.title: Orforglipron (Foundayo): Heart-Safe vs Insulin? ACHIEVE-4 #shorts
package.description:
In ACHIEVE-4, orforglipron (Foundayo) wasn't worse than insulin glargine for major heart events in adults with type 2 diabetes, overweight/obesity and higher heart risk: 4.2% vs 5.0% over ~2 years (HR 0.84, CI crosses 1 — not proven better). Stomach side effects were more common on the pill. This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Is the orforglipron pill (Foundayo) heart-safe? A big trial in type 2 diabetes just reported.

ACHIEVE-4 followed 2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes, overweight or obesity, and higher heart risk for about 2 years, comparing the orforglipron pill (Foundayo) to insulin glargine. Major heart events happened in 4.2% on the pill vs 5.0% on insulin — a hazard ratio of 0.84, but the statistical range crosses 1, so this means "not worse than insulin," not "proven better." There was also a lower rate of all-cause deaths on the pill, but since that wasn't the trial's main goal, it's a hint worth watching, not proof. Keep in mind: this was open-label, compared against insulin rather than a placebo, and funded by Lilly. Stomach side effects were more common on the pill. As of September 2026, it's approved for weight management in the US and UK, and for type 2 diabetes in the UK. It's not yet approved for type 2 diabetes in the US.

script.working_title: Is the Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill Safe for Your Heart? ACHIEVE-4 vs Insulin Glargine #shorts
script.hook_pattern: Search-style question that names the drug people know, generic name first with the brand for recognition. It's answered within about 15 s with the verified randomized population, comparator, absolute rates and timeframe. Then come an evidence-literacy myth-bust ("not worse ≠ proven better"), an honestly hedged extra finding, the limits, the date-hedged approval status (US: weight management only, as of Sept 2026) and the stomach side effects. It loops back to the opening "heart-safe?" question with the full population and ends on the exact prescriber line. Narration is trimmed to about 167 words to stay under the hard maximum.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the key facts against the Lilly/PR Newswire release (30 Sept 2026), the MedicalXpress report of the Lancet paper, the MHRA notice of 10 Aug 2026, the FDA non-inferiority guidance (2016) and coverage of the FDA approval on 1 Apr 2026. They confirm:
- 2,749 randomized (1,371 on orforglipron vs 1,378 on insulin glargine), open-label, Lilly-funded.
- MACE-4 was 4.2% vs 5.0% over a median of about 2 years, HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.59–1.20), with a non-inferiority margin of 1.8.
- All-cause death HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.25–0.75), not controlled for multiplicity.
- Stomach (GI) side effects 62.1% vs 14.2%.
- Approval status: US weight management only; UK weight management plus type 2 diabetes.

The science and framing are mostly strong: absolute rates, comparator, population, non-inferiority explained correctly, and the death result is hedged.

Fixable problems:
1. The all-cause death result is given only as a relative HR, with no absolute figures. Our craft rules require the absolute numbers for every relative figure.
2. The US approval claim in s7 has no cited source.
3. "Nominal P=.002" couldn't be verified.
4. The title's "Safe for Your Heart?" reaches beyond the trial population. The paywalled Lancet title isn't confirmed either.

Nothing here is unsafe, and the prescriber line appears correctly in s8 and the CTA.

issues.claim: Bonus: all-cause deaths were lower, hazard ratio 0.43. Not a main goal, so a hint, not proof.
issues.problem: The relative figure (HR 0.43) has no absolute rates. MedicalXpress, reporting the Lancet paper, gives 19/1,371 (1.4%) vs 43/1,355 (3.2%). Our rule is that every relative figure needs its absolute figure, and a bare HR 0.43 invites a '57% fewer deaths' reading.
issues.fix: Narration: "Bonus: deaths from any cause were 1.4% vs 3.2%, hazard ratio 0.43. Not a main goal, so a hint, not proof." Change stat_value to "1.4% vs 3.2%" and stat_label to "All-cause death, ~2 yrs (HR 0.43): not a main goal". Keep on_screen_text "Deaths: a hint only".

issues.problem: The CI and the 'not controlled for multiplicity' point are confirmed by the Lilly release. The nominal P=.002 isn't in any reachable source.
issues.fix: Replace with: "All-cause death 1.4% vs 3.2% (19/1,371 vs 43/1,355); HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.25–0.75). Not a main goal; not controlled for multiplicity; hypothesis-generating. ACHIEVE-4, The Lancet 2026; Lilly release 30 Sept 2026". Add src6 to source_ids.

issues.problem: No cited source covers the US approval date. src5 says only that it's FDA-approved for weight management and investigational for T2D. The 1 Apr 2026 date is confirmed by press coverage (TIME) but isn't cited.
issues.fix: Add source src7: "FDA Approves Eli Lilly's Obesity Pill, Foundayo", TIME, 2026, https://time.com/article/2026/04/01/fda-approves-eli-lilly-obesity-pill/. Add src7 to s7 source_ids.

issues.claim: Is the Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill Safe for Your Heart?
issues.problem: "Your heart" generalizes to every viewer. The trial only showed non-inferiority vs insulin glargine in adults with T2D, overweight/obesity and higher cardiovascular risk (85.9% had established CVD). The Short answers this correctly, but the title promises more.

issues.problem: This is accurate, but it's vague when a verified figure is available (62.1% vs 14.2%).
issues.fix: "Stomach side effects were more common on the pill: 62.1% vs 14.2%." If the word budget is tight, put the numbers in an on-screen pill instead.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits well within target under voice (-13.5dB) but ran a touch hot in pauses (-12.7 vs ~-14 target), so trimmed overall by ~1.4dB (gain 0.85). Thinned three overlapping SFX clusters (56.5-58s, 62.7-64s, 85.1-85.5s) that exceeded the 3-4-effects-per-second guideline by dropping redundant blips/swooshes and pulling down a couple of speech-bed blips that were sitting too loud (-11 to -13dB) back toward the -16dB felt zone. Added three bespoke heartbeat/chime accents to underline the cardiovascular framing and the reassuring close without adding extra stock pops.
